subject: learning: anytime-valid betting test for SHADOW_DIRECT (ORDRE 12b)
body:
learning: anytime-valid betting test for SHADOW_DIRECT (ORDRE 12b)

anytime_valid_mean_test(values, lower, upper, alpha, beta, h1_mean,
max_observations, *, groups=None): testing by betting (Waudby-Smith &
Ramdas 2023), truncated aGRAPA bet, cap 0.9 of the admissible range, prior
pseudo-round at h1/2 with variance ((upper-lower)/2)^2. ACCEPT_EDGE at
wealth >= 1/alpha against mean <= 0, REJECT_EDGE at wealth >= 1/beta
against mean >= h1 (REJECT wins ties), INCONCLUSIVE at the horizon. Valid by
Ville's inequality given only bounds and conditional mean <= 0 given
earlier ROUNDS. Pure and final. Existing functions are unchanged.

Finding: betting per match is NOT valid under common evening shocks,
because the conditional-mean condition fails inside an evening. The
optional `groups` key makes one bet per evening: any dependence is allowed
inside a round. The cost is power, because a round is worth one bounded
observation.

Seeded validation, alpha 0.025, 20 000 H0 paths per scenario, horizon 2000.
False ACCEPT, new/match | new/evening | old t-SPRT:
  normal 0.0021|0|0.0212  t3 0.0014|0|0.0135  rare_loss 0.0040|0|0.0032
  evening_shock 0.0826|0|0.1950  vol_drift 0.0052|0|0.0231
Per evening at horizon 12 000 (QUANT_SLOW_TESTS=1): 0 in all five.
H1 (0.00475, sigma 0.05): iid per match, power 0.991 with median 1254
matches (old: 0.950 / 648). Evening shocks per evening: power 1.000 with
median 8159 matches (p90 10837, 82% by 10 000). Old t-SPRT: 0.710 power
with 0.290 false REJECT. All fixtures are synthetic, not market evidence.

fingerprint/earliest-recorded-at instead of the session under evaluation,
which is a real forward-confirmation laundering vector under ordinary
ledger growth; and LearningStore's 200-entry persisted lesson window
breaks record_research's (and the proposed record_economic_outcome's)
replay idempotence once total lessons exceed that window.

schemas or workflows touched; no branch merged or cherry-picked.

subject: fix: close F11 whole-parent-directory replacement (F11-P1/P2/P3)
body:
fix: close F11 whole-parent-directory replacement (F11-P1/P2/P3)

Bind Registry mutation to the parent-directory fd captured at lock
acquisition (dir_fd-relative opens/reads/writes for the lock, its
hard-link authority anchor, and the registry file) instead of
re-resolving pathnames during the critical section, and add a
grandparent-anchored marker recording the one directory inode first
bootstrapped for a configured registry parent. A replacement directory
swapped in at the same pathname is now recognized as ambiguous and
rejected before any mutation, closing the gap where a whole-parent
replacement while a holder was active could otherwise let a second
process bootstrap an independent registry history concurrently.

Adds real-subprocess F11-P1/P2/P3 tests reproducing Blue's exact
whole-parent-replacement challenge; confirmed RED against the
pre-repair implementation and GREEN after.

subject: fix(p0): canonicalize ExecStart to stop effective-unit digest drift
body:
fix(p0): canonicalize ExecStart to stop effective-unit digest drift

Target-host evidence (defect artifact sha256:cb402bb3...442) showed
_effective_systemd_definition hashing the raw `ExecStart` show property.
On real systemd that property mixes static command configuration with
transient execution observations (start_time/stop_time/pid/code/status),
so the acquisition-critical digest moved every time the qualifying
service actually ran even though nothing semantic changed. That could
make a valid pre-start materialization fail fingerprint validation
purely from the service having executed.

Parse ExecStart into structured entries, drop the transient observation
keys, and bind the configuration-only form (path/argv/ignore_errors)
into the digest instead of the raw string. Also tighten the qualifying
flag check from a substring test to an exact argv-token match, since a
substring check would silently accept an altered flag such as
`--qualifying-disabled` as if qualifying were still present.

Adds Phase8EffectiveUnitDigestStabilityCampaign covering every
discriminant required by the mission spec: transient-metadata stability,
same-unit before/after invocation stability, path/argv drift, qualifying
flag removal/alteration, drop-ins, fragment byte mismatch, workdir/env
drift, unparseable ExecStart, and an end-to-end materialize/authorize
digest-stability check via _effective_environment.

Regenerated STATE.md's proof-inventory count (411 -> 423) to match the
12 added tests; status_artifacts.py --check and generate_schemas.py
--check both pass.

Adds EconomicAssessmentJournal (append-only, idempotent by
assessment_id+input_fingerprint, conflict-detecting on a different

subject: data: manual capture runner, and a real live capture proves the pipeline works
body:
data: manual capture runner, and a real live capture proves the pipeline works

Adds scripts/forward_capture_runner.py (mission section 6/7): declare-universe/
declare-sessions/run-once/status/coverage, each a thin wrapper calling exactly
forward_capture.due/execute_forward_capture and forward_coverage.* -- no logic
of its own beyond argument parsing. This is the same contract a future
Control Plane change would call. paths.py gains a forward subtree (not on the
mission's forbidden list; only clock.py, scripts/quant.py and sec/** are),
mirroring the existing sec_* convention.

Ran it for real against the live Yahoo endpoint: declare-sessions seeded
2,514 real trading sessions from the committed us_sector_etf_daily snapshot;
run-once made one real HTTP fetch and durably recorded 60 real observations
(12 symbols x 5 sessions newer than the static snapshot's own last date, so
they could not have been read from it) with full provenance; a forced
re-attempt over the identical window produced 0 newly-accepted, proving
idempotent resubmission live. Evidence in
handoff/FORWARD_DATA_FIRST_LIVE_CAPTURE_2026-09-20.json.

Two more real gaps found by running the actual tool, not by inspection:
(1) ForwardCoverageLedger.summary()'s inner loop iterated
expected_symbols_for(session) or (), which silently skipped any session
older than a universe declaration's effective_from instead of reporting it
UNKNOWN -- against the real 2,514-session calendar this made the whole
report show all-zero counts. Fixed by enumerating every declared session
against every symbol ever declared (ExpectedCalendar.all_declared_symbols,
new) and letting classify() resolve each cell, with a regression test.
(2) That fix made summary() O(cells x file-scans) -- correct but
impractically slow at 30,168 cells; fixed by computing the accepted/
conflict/attempt indexes once per call and threading them through classify()'s
new optional keyword arguments (unmeasured/slow -> ~0.15-0.8s).

A third, operational-only gap: the static dataset's calendar stops at its
own last ingested date, so newly observed sessions could not classify as
VALID until declared. Closed honestly: run-once now also declares the exact
sessions its own successful payload contained as expected -- a retroactive
record of an observed fact, never a forward-looking claim, and it never
touches any attempt's own success/failure outcome. summary(session_from=...)/
`coverage --since` was added so a status check can focus on the
operationally relevant window instead of the honest but UNKNOWN-heavy
multi-year tail.

6 new tests. Full suite: 654 passed, 0 regressions.

economic: refuse a syntactic-only PROVENANCE_CALIBRATED claim

Adds ProvenanceBinding (version, as_of, authority, dataset_fingerprint,
artifact_hash, validation_state) to EconomicParameter and a new
ParameterInventory.bind_provenance(), layered on top of instantiate()
without changing its signature. Wired into MEUERecipe._consumability(): a
parameter claiming PROVENANCE_CALIBRATED (the only class that can make a
recipe RECIPE_CONSUMABLE) without a bound ProvenanceBinding now downgrades
the recipe to RECIPE_PROVISIONAL with a new note, the same treatment the
method already gives an uncalibrated execution parameter or an unfrozen
margin functional. Only PROVENANCE_CALIBRATED is held to this bar --
PROVENANCE_V1_ASSUMED/ENGINEERING_BOUND already admit non-authoritative
status and are charged as model risk instead.

Closes two independently-found defects: Wave 1 red team item 4
(ExposureBudget provenance is declared, not proved) and Codex's self red
team item 5 (a nonempty source string can lie). provenance_binding is
excluded from ParameterInventory.rule_document(), so it cannot change a
recipe's fingerprint -- it is value-adjacent evidence, not part of the
frozen rule.

Deliberately not wired as an always-on structural violation: that would
have broken ~75 pre-existing Wave 1 tests whose shared fixture's default
recipe already mixes calibrated and V1-assumed parameters. One existing
test needed a minimal, honest update (bind_provenance added to its already
fully-calibrated fixture; its RECIPE_CONSUMABLE assertion is unchanged).
618/618 tests pass (588 Wave 1 + 30 this pass).

Adds forward_admissibility.py (mission section 9), zero changes to Wave 1's
admissibility.py. forward_dataset_view() renders a ForwardRecorder as a
registry-record-shaped dict for evaluate_admissibility; recorded_from is the
recorder's own earliest accepted write (new ForwardRecorder.

A second real gap found by testing section 9's own stated invariant ("une
version deja utilisee pour fit ne devient jamais forward confirmation"):
evaluate_admissibility's FORWARD_CONFIRMATION branch checks only timing and
the pre-outcome seal, never the UseLedger's fit/validation history for that
version -- so a version already spent on EXPLORATORY_FIT could still

racing an empty/older file can each locally accept a different value for the
same brand-new key, because each one's in-memory guard only knows about writes
it has itself made or already replayed. The prior accepted()/__init__ read
path did not re-enforce first-accepted-per-key across such a race, so a third,
freshly opened reader could see two different ACCEPTED rows for one key --
exactly the incoherent history the mission's failure model forbids. Fixed with
one _replay() every reader now goes through: first accepted content address
per key wins in append order, and every later, differently-addressed row for
that key is surfaced via a new race_conflicts() accessor instead of silently
returned as a second valid observation. History already on disk is never
rewritten -- this is a read-time reclassification.

delivery tolerated while ledger order is enforced, timezone-offset
normalisation at the monotonicity boundary, torn/partial final write recovery,
the two-writer race and its identical-value non-race control, vendor

subject: research: second independent family, prioritisation, operational failure modelling
body:
research: second independent family, prioritisation, operational failure modelling

Research side.

factory/families.py declares a family whose signal never reads the asset's own
return. For each name it aggregates the trailing returns of that name's most
correlated peers: sectors share factors but absorb information at different
speeds, so a name that has not moved with its peers either catches up or the
peers overreacted. That is a different mechanism from own-residual reversal, not
a re-parameterisation of it, which is what breadth means here. Peers are chosen
on a correlation window that *ends before* the signal window opens, so peer
selection cannot use the returns the signal is made of; a test perturbs only the
signal window and asserts the selected peer sets are unchanged while the scores
move. Independence is declared on named structural axes and then checked against
the other family's realised score vectors, and a declared independence that
fails empirically reports FAMILIES_EMPIRICALLY_COLLINEAR rather than standing.

The lane is declared in full — mechanism, falsification bar, grid, trial count —
but deliberately not added to lanes.lane_definitions, because that changes what
clock.py schedules and clock.py is fingerprint-critical for P0 in this wave. The
dispatch lives in families.weights_for_family and the integration point is
documented in the module. Declaring the grid now means its 48 trials are
countable against the family-wise budget before anything is run.

factory/prioritization.py ranks hypotheses on declared inputs: information value
and capital potential over Builder days and sessions to falsification. The
formula is crude on purpose; what matters is what it may not read. Any
prospective P0 signal in the priority inputs is refused with
P0_RESERVOIR_IS_NEVER_A_PRIORITY_SIGNAL, because prioritising research by what
the reservoir seems to contain is the same leak as reading it, only slower. An
inadmissible candidate has no priority rather than a low one, and a candidate
whose prerequisites are unsatisfied is refused because work on it now would
produce evidence nothing can consume.

Operations side (src/quant/operations).

failures.py models the failures that corrupt economic state quietly rather than
crashing loudly. A stale quote cannot mark or size, and a quote timestamped ahead
of the valuation instant is stale too, because disagreeing clocks would value a
position on information the decision could not have had. A missing or NaN bar
blocks the decision instead of being forward-filled into one; a halt blocks it
even when a bar exists. Order submission is write-ahead: the client order id is
reserved and journaled before anything is sent, so a crash in between leaves
evidence and a restart suppresses the resubmission rather than doubling the
exposure and its frictions. Fills accumulate by fill id, duplicates are ignored
and an overfill past the intended quantity is refused. After an outage,
reconciliation returns RECONCILIATION_UNKNOWN: the ledger does not decide that an
unreachable order filled, or that it did not.

readiness.py is capital-readiness V3 as five separate gates — statistical
evidence, economic sufficiency after frictions, capacity headroom, operational
failure handling, monitoring. It reports the weakest gate rather than an average,
since an average lets strong statistics cover for absent capacity. A gate nobody
assessed is missing, not passed, and a satisfied gate needs an evidence
reference. The best state reachable is PAPER_SHADOW_READY; real capital is not a
state the system may assign itself.

monitoring.py applies a retirement rule that must have been declared before the
first window it judges, since deciding afterwards what counts as decay is a
negotiation with a losing position. Consecutive breaches retire, scattered
breaches drift, and realised friction above the declared drift limit is reported
as capacity erosion.

registry.py is the evidence registry: dataset version, protocol hash, code SHA,
result and decision, idempotent on the chain hash. A record missing any link is
refused and journaled as incomplete, because a partial provenance chain looks
like evidence and is worse than none.

protocol: closed D07 semantics executable, D05-A invariance test, ratio inference

src/quant/science implements decisions that governance/ has already closed and
parameterises the dimensions those artifacts leave open. It decides nothing: an
undeclared open dimension returns a state, never a default that would quietly
select a geometry.

eligibility.py — the closed D07 s2.1 population as a predicate: original Form 4
only, non-derivative, transaction code P with acquired indicator A, reporting
owner director and/or officer, ten-percent status alone insufficient. The
notation trap gets its own test: Form 4 code A is an award, indicator A means
acquired, and a qualifying purchase is code P *with* indicator A. Pooling code
A would put compensation grants into a conviction-buying population.

formation.py — the closed signal geometry. Rolling window of ten regular
sessions over distinct qualifying insider CIKs, threshold crossing <2 -> >=2,
no repeated formation while the window is active, re-arm only once it falls
below two, and expiry as a session-boundary transition evaluated before any
observation attached to that session. The discriminating test for
WINDOW_EXPIRY_PRECEDES_SESSION_ADDITIONS is included: owner A at session 0 and
owner B at session 10 must produce no formation, and would produce one if
additions ran before expiry. Entry is the first session strictly after the
EDGAR date, never same day, and the hold is twenty sessions.

O1 is the frozen exhaustive set {PREVIOUS_REGULAR_SESSION, NEXT_REGULAR_SESSION};
NEAREST_REGULAR_SESSION is refused by name. O2 takes a caller-declared
deterministic ordering and this module does not enumerate an admissible set,
because D07 does not. O3 declares interval indexing only: an offset that would
change the closed twenty-session hold is refused, and an unobservable session
inside the interval routes to D19_TERMINAL_TREATMENT_REQUIRED rather than
receiving any payoff substitute. Until O4 is declared, an observation count is
D05_B_UNTIL_O4_FROZEN instead of a number.

invariance.py — the D05-A design-invariance test of D07 s5, executable. A
quantity is run over every admissible combination of O1 x O2 x O3 x O4; equal
values are DESIGN_INVARIANT_D05A_ELIGIBLE, differing values are
CLAIM_DESIGN_SENSITIVE_D05B, and anything undefined or unresolved under some
admissible convention is AMBIGUOUS_EMBARGO. The space actually used is returned
with the verdict, so a narrowed space is visible rather than implied. A worked
case shows a weekend EDGAR date straddling the window boundary, where one
admissible O1 convention forms a signal and the other does not.

inference.py — the ratio estimator with a random denominator. Cluster-robust
delta-method variance with the usual small-cluster inflation, plus a
seed-declared cluster bootstrap. A test shows that correctly clustering
overlapping exposures widens the interval, which is the free t-statistic that
PRIMITIVE_RETURN_VARIANCE_IS_NOT_AGGREGATE_ESTIMATOR_VARIANCE warns about. The
multiplicity budget may be widened with disclosure and never narrowed. The
statistical and economic questions are answered separately and reported
together, so a significant effect entirely below MEUE reads as significant and
economically dominated rather than as a pass.

nulls.py — nulls that preserve the structure not under test. The placebo shift
refuses an offset landing inside the true exposure window, since an overlapping
placebo shares returns with the real holding period and understates the null
spread. Cluster sign-flipping flips whole clusters, never observations inside
one. Empirical p-values use (1 + hits) / (1 + draws) and are never zero.

regimes.py — a regime partition carries the instant it was declared and the
input classes it was built from; outcome-bearing inputs or a declaration at or
after outcome observation are refused as POST_HOC_REGIME_SELECTION_REFUSED. The
pooled estimate is the headline and per-regime figures are diagnostics:
BEST_REGIME_IS_NOT_THE_RESULT.

subject: data: forward recorder, Form 4 structure extraction, dataset admissibility
body:
data: forward recorder, Form 4 structure extraction, dataset admissibility

Three additions on the data side, none of which touches the P0 SEC capture
package or reads its reservoir.

Forward recorder (dataplane/forward_recorder.py). Every historical result this
system can produce is development evidence, because the data already existed
when the hypothesis was written. Evidence that is out of sample by
construction requires recording market state now and using it later, so the
store is forward-only in wall clock (an observation recorded before the latest
one already stored is refused), immutable (a differing value for the same
symbol/session/field set is journaled as a conflict instead of overwriting, so
a vendor restatement stays visible), and point-in-time readable through as_of,
which returns only what was recorded strictly before a given instant. Coverage
reports COVERAGE_UNKNOWN unless an independent expected calendar and universe
are supplied; completeness is never asserted unasked. session_seal publishes a
per-session hash so the record can later prove it existed before an outcome
window opened. The recorder stores observations handed to it, each with a
source and source fingerprint, and invents nothing.

Form 4 structure extraction (dataplane/form4_parse.py). A pure function over
bytes with no filesystem or network access, so it is structurally unable to
read the P0 capture reservoir; development fixtures are synthetic. Three
modelling decisions carry most of the value. A grant (code A) is not an
open-market purchase (code P): is_open_market_purchase is narrow on purpose,
because pooling them measures compensation schedules alongside conviction
buying. A footnote-only price is PRICE_IN_FOOTNOTE_NOT_MACHINE_READABLE, never
0.0. And periodOfReport is not when the market could know: the parser refuses
to supply a public-observability instant at all, reporting
PUBLIC_OBSERVABILITY_REQUIRES_ACCEPTANCE_TIMESTAMP, since that instant lives
outside the document. Malformed input returns a state rather than raising, so
a pipeline keeps the evidence that a filing was malformed.

Dataset admissibility (dataplane/admissibility.py). The four uses the mission
separates — discovery, exploratory fit, validation, forward confirmation — are
only separated if something enforces it across runs. UseLedger is a durable
one-way ratchet keyed on dataset version (id plus fingerprint): validation on
a version already fitted is refused, while a refreshed fingerprint is a new
version and therefore new evidence. No historical dataset can serve as forward
confirmation, however carefully held back, because it existed before the
protocol was frozen and could have shaped it; forward confirmation also
requires a pre-outcome seal. Admissibility is decided from provenance and use
history alone, before any value is read.

subject: execution: event causal timeline, opening-regime fills, economic sizing
body:
execution: event causal timeline, opening-regime fills, economic sizing

Four additions that close the rest of the Economic Engine's first draft, and
one defect found while building them.

Causal timeline (src/quant/economics/timeline.py). The V1 desk already runs
one session timeline; an event lane needs the same discipline per event. Every
decision input carries the instant it became available, and a decision that
consumed an input from its own future is LOOKAHEAD_INPUT_NOT_YET_AVAILABLE.
Dates and timestamps are normalised to one UTC scale first, because a bare
date compared as a string is how an off-by-one-session lookahead hides. Entry
before public observability, a fill before the first authorized open and a
Book mark before the fill are all refused. NetOutcome charges frictions once:
a return already net of deployment frictions is refused as the coordinate
(DELTA_IS_GROSS_OF_FORM4_DEPLOYMENT_FRICTIONS), and research evidence that
charged less than execution is refused too. Aggregation is the exposure-
weighted ratio with its denominator reported, since the denominator is random.
CausalEventLedger is idempotent per (event, stage) and replays to the same
state after a crash, including a torn final append.

Opening-regime execution (opening.py). Entry at the first authorized open is
an explicit modelling dimension. The overnight gap from prior close to open is
market return and belongs to T_j, so it is reported and labelled, never
charged: measuring execution loss against the prior close returns
OPEN_EXECUTION_COST_MUST_NOT_DOUBLE_COUNT_MARKET_RETURN. Coefficients carry
the regime they were calibrated on, and applying an intraday calibration to
the opening auction is a violation rather than a silent substitution.

Sizing (sizing.py). Exposure is a declared monotone function of the margin of
safety over MEUE, not an optimum found by search. Relative weights are scaled
and never reshaped. A plan records its ordered transforms and hashes its final
state; an approval taken against an earlier state is refused
(RISK_APPROVAL_MUST_DESCRIBE_FINAL_PORTFOLIO), and a plan marked final cannot
be transformed again. Per-strategy sleeves stay separate while the aggregate
view serves portfolio limits.

DEFECT ECON-001 — RESEARCH_COST_ASSUMPTION_UNDERSTATES_MODELLED_EXECUTION.
src/quant/desk/execution.py states the desk model "is calibrated to land at or
under" RESEARCH_ONE_WAY_COST_BPS = 5.0. Reading the shipped coefficients, the
desk's one-way cost is 0.5 + 1.0 + 10.0*sqrt(participation/0.05), which equals
11.5 bps at the desk's own max_participation of 5% — a 6.5 bps understatement.
The research assumption is only covered below 0.6125% of ADV, 8.2x below the
desk limit, and the 2x cost stress test in factory/evaluate.py (10 bps) does
not reach it either. RESEARCH_ONE_WAY_COST_BPS is also never imported: the
research charge is a separate literal (factory/lanes.py COST_BPS = 5.0), so
nothing was checking the documented relationship.

consistency.py makes the relationship executable: it computes the implied
participation ceiling from the desk model's own fields and blocks the economic
gate when research evidence is cheaper than the executable path. Neither
constant is changed here. Which one moves is a research-protocol decision,
because raising the research cost re-rates already recorded lane evidence
while lowering desk participation does not, and that choice belongs to the
project owner rather than to this branch.

subject: economic: executable MEUE recipe engine (D09 Route-B mini-core)
body:
economic: executable MEUE recipe engine (D09 Route-B mini-core)

Adds src/quant/economics: the mechanical, outcome-blind chain from a
scientific effect to a CONTINUE / NO_TRADE / KILL verdict, built on the
frozen Route-B D09 contracts rather than alongside them.

What is now executable rather than prose:

- DELTA_COORDINATE_COMPATIBILITY_GATE with its three states. Undeclared
  beats mismatched; a mismatch reopens the accounting implementation
  instead of bending EC1's coordinate to fit available data.
- Parameter inventory with a per-parameter source contract. Freezing hashes
  the rule with central values stripped, so RULE_BEFORE_VALUES is checkable
  and a cost absent from the frozen inventory cannot be inserted later.
  A value carrying only ASSUMED_V1_EXECUTION_PARAMETER provenance is
  refused unless its model risk is charged in M_economic, which is how
  EXISTING_EXECUTION_PARAMETER_IS_NOT_AUTOMATIC_CALIBRATION_AUTHORITY
  becomes a failing check.
- K_forward as a recipe with the nine mandatory declarations per component.
  Only CENTRAL_EXPECTATION estimators are admissible and any prudential
  markup is refused (NO_HIDDEN_CONSERVATISM_INSIDE_K_FORWARD). Every class
  F1..F7 must be modelled or explicitly authorised zero
  (OMITTED_COST_IS_NOT_IMPLICIT_ZERO). Declared dependence is probed
  numerically, so a component that secretly varies with delta cannot reach
  the affine BEEE shortcut.
- Phi and BEEE with the four root states, a declared effect domain and a
  deterministic bisection. The affine quotient K/Q is available only when
  Q > 0 and cost independence actually holds, checked not assumed.
- Joint cost scenarios S_cost. There is no code path that sums marginal
  envelopes; M_economic = max over adverse scenarios of the BEEE increment,
  labelled FREEZE_CANDIDATE_NOT_AUTHORITY per the cost/scenario contract.
  An adverse scenario that moves a parameter to its favourable side, or
  that leaves an uncalibrated coefficient unperturbed, blocks the margin.
- Anti-double-counting map: one risk class, one economic home, or a
  documented non-overlap decomposition. Program/Builder/research cost and
  statistical uncertainty cannot be claimed at all.
- theta sealed ahead of the threshold: an EvaluationSession refuses a new
  capital point after a threshold has been produced
  (NO_SIZE_SEARCH_TO_MAKE_MEUE_ATTAINABLE).
- Capacity as a first-order object. Uneven clipping is reported as
  CAPACITY_CLIPPING_THAT_CHANGES_RELATIVE_WEIGHTS_IS_NEW_POLICY_VERSION
  rather than as a smaller position, and a name with no liquidity reference
  is granted nothing instead of being presumed infinitely liquid.
- The economic gate. A statistically significant effect whose whole
  plausible interval sits below MEUE returns KILL; undeclared residual beta
  or a straddling interval returns NO_TRADE. Every verdict carries
  PAPER_SHADOW_ONLY.

No numerical Form-4 cost coefficient is asserted in src/. The illustrative
values live in tests/economics_fixtures.py and are labelled as fixtures with
no scientific authority. RECIPE_CONSUMABLE is unreachable while any consumed
parameter lacks calibration authority or the margin functional remains a
freeze candidate, so the engine reports RECIPE_PROVISIONAL for the current
state of the governance record.

subject: p0: make the systemd start cause unambiguous and verify the materialized fingerprint
body:
p0: make the systemd start cause unambiguous and verify the materialized fingerprint

Blue's two follow-up points on PR #17, both accepted. Closing the second exposed a
third gap, also closed.

SYSTEMD_RESTART_CAUSE_AMBIGUOUS - CLOSED
INVOCATION_ID proves systemd launched the service but not why, so
`systemctl restart quant-sec-capture` typed by a human classified as
SCHEDULED_START and hid an operator intervention behind a non-invalidating cause.

An automatic action must now be positively demonstrated. Being launched by a
service manager is not such a demonstration. The only positive reasons a cleanly
stopped service can start are a host boot - visible because the kernel's boot id
at /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id changed, a fact an operator cannot omit - and
the first start of a deployment, which is not a restart "after a stop or failure"
and so not an intervention under §5.2. A restart after a failure counts as
automatic only while it is inside the window the unit's RestartSec implies; past
that systemd has stopped retrying, so a new start is an operator acting on a
stopped service. Everything else, including a malformed state with no exit
timestamp, is MANUAL_START - the safe direction, because it is the answer that
invalidates the window.

Verified live: a clean prior stop, the same host boot id and a new invocation
identity - exactly what systemctl restart looks like - was classified MANUAL_START
and recorded as invalidating.

MATERIALIZED_FINGERPRINT_NOT_VERIFIED_AGAINST_ACTIVE - CLOSED
t0_readiness() checked only that the fingerprint file existed, never that it
described the running build. That is how a stale fingerprint reached a published
rodage artifact while visibility.py - explicitly fingerprint-critical - had changed
after it was computed. The artifact carried sha256:6f516b66 while the head's true
fingerprint was sha256:0fa9ab55, and nothing compared them.

Readiness and telemetry now compare the materialized fingerprint against the active
one and block on FINGERPRINT_MATERIALIZED_MISMATCH. Existence alone is no longer
accepted, because a manifest describing a different build is worse than none: it
presents a frozen state the service does not have.

The check earned its keep immediately. A manifest materialized outside the service
environment can never match, because effective service configuration is part of the
manifest - so a hand-run sec-fingerprint produces a freeze the service will always
reject. The supervisor now materializes the manifest itself, in the exact child
environment, and only when none exists. Never overwriting is the point: a
deployment that changes acquisition semantics has to surface as a mismatch rather
than silently re-freeze itself mid-window. sec-fingerprint also prints the effective
service invocation it froze, so a hand-run is visibly context-dependent.

SERVICE_ENTRY_POINT_OUTSIDE_FINGERPRINT - found by Builder, CLOSED
BLOCKS_CAPTURE_INTEGRITY. scripts/quant.py was not in ACQUISITION_CRITICAL_MODULES,
yet its sec-serve command binds the clock's wake cadence into system.serve() and so
decides how often a due poll is noticed. A change to the service entry point could
have altered acquisition timing without moving the fingerprint. Added to the frozen
membership, and the verification tree digest now covers deploy/ as well since the
unit and launcher are fingerprint-critical. Membership may only be narrowed before
the first qualifying t0, so it is widened while that is still permitted.

Final rodage: handoff/SEC_FORM4_P0_PRE_T0_RODAGE_FINAL_2026-09-19.json, run on the
exact frozen state and superseding both earlier rodage artifacts. Its generator
aborts if the active and materialized fingerprints differ, so a stale value cannot
be published again. Fingerprint
sha256:b84925b8474702fe86e60110f941b7096e991ebb880d6a3cfc0001d35741e976, materialized
by the supervisor and equal to the active one. Readiness reports ready with no
blockers. Coverage COMPLETE with no open gap. The audit reports
INVALIDATING_INTERVENTION, which is the correct outcome: the rodage deliberately
performed the operator-restart falsification, and a window that intervenes is not a
candidate.

21 new tests. Operator restart, host reboot, first deployment start, automatic
restart inside and outside the window, dead supervisor inside and outside the
window, malformed state, deployment precedence, and the kernel boot id read itself;
plus nothing materialized, a stale manifest, telemetry surfacing the mismatch,
re-materializing clearing it, and a changed acquisition module making it stale end
to end.

310 tests pass, 206 in the SEC P0 lane.

t0 is NOT declared. P0_CONTINUOUS_SERVICE_STATE remains
OPEN / NOT_YET_PROVEN_CONTINUOUS. Merge authority and t0 belong to Blue.

subject: p0: close VISIBILITY_FIREWALL_REGRESSION, add verification provenance, second rodage
body:
p0: close VISIBILITY_FIREWALL_REGRESSION, add verification provenance, second rodage

Blue findings 3 and 4, plus two further defects of the same class found while
remediating and two rodage results.

VISIBILITY_FIREWALL_REGRESSION - CLOSED, exposure irreversible
The artifact published attempts_by_endpoint_kind.FILING = 7 while asserting it
carried no filing count. Under the frozen path one filing costs one FILING
request, so that integer was a filing count by proxy. Blue observed it.

The value and its siblings (result-state and per-second request tallies, from
which it could also be derived) are removed, and the invariant they were meant to
evidence is now stated without volume: REQUEST_ACCOUNTING_INVARIANT = PASS,
UNACCOUNTED_NETWORK_REQUESTS = FALSE, DUPLICATED_ATTEMPT_AUTHORITY = FALSE. A
visibility_firewall_provenance block records that the exposure happened, that Blue
saw it, that it is irreversible, that blindness was NOT restored, and that it has
no authority over any later scientific decision.

A prose promise is not a control, so find_count_proxies now walks a structured
payload for the shape of the defect - any numeric field whose key marks it as a
count of filings or of the per-filing request class - and the artifact cannot make
the same claim alongside the same number again.

DRAIN_TRANSITION_COUNT_PROXY - found by Builder, CLOSED
The same artifact also published transition_causes.DRAIN_COMPLETED and
transition_states.DRAINING as integers. The drain path completes once per acquired
filing, so both were the filing count under another name. The first detector missed
them because their key names mention no filings. Per-cause and per-state tallies
are replaced by the sorted set of causes and states observed, and the detector
matches drain and capture keys on the full path. Blue saw these too, so this
exposure is equally irreversible.

FIREWALL_TIER_CONTRACT_OVERSTATED - found by Builder, CLOSED
paths.sec_firewall_safe_journals() was documented as "capture state a
protocol-mutating surface is allowed to read", with the scheduler and attempt
journals in it. Those journals carry no filing-identifying string, but they are
per-event records and some events are one per filing, so counting them recovers the
count. The name asserted a guarantee the contents did not provide, which is why a
per-cause tally reached a published artifact without anyone noticing what it was.
Renamed sec_operator_internal_journals() with the guarantee stated exactly: no
identifying content, volume inferable, not publishable as they stand. The no-count
rule binds the published projection - status surface, Chief Brief, telemetry, the
observation audit and the committed artifacts - and a test holds that set to it.
No new disclosure; this is the contract-clarity defect behind the other two.

subject: p0: close LIFECYCLE_PROVENANCE_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE
body:
p0: close LIFECYCLE_PROVENANCE_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE

Blue finding 2, accepted in full. Three separate ways the start cause could still
be wrong, each closed.

A. Omission can no longer buy a clean record.
The old design derived MANUAL_START from an --manual flag, so a human who simply
did not pass it was recorded as SCHEDULED_START. The default direction is now
inverted: classification starts from service-manager provenance, and a launch that
cannot show a recognised manager plus its per-invocation identity is MANUAL_START
and non-qualifying, whatever flags were passed. The unit declares
QUANT_SEC_SERVICE_MANAGER=systemd and systemd supplies INVOCATION_ID per
invocation; both are required. A human can of course export those deliberately,
which is forgery and no environment check prevents it - what is removed is the
omission path, which is what Blue's finding was about. --manual survives only so an
operator can be explicit: it can make a launch manual, never scheduled.

B. The supervisor's own death is visible.
Durable state now records that a supervisor is running and under which invocation
identity, set before the child launches and cleared only on a clean exit. A new
supervisor that finds a previous one still marked running under a different
identity reports AUTOMATIC_RESTART_AFTER_SUPERVISOR_FAILURE. Previously that case
read the last_child_exit_code=null written just before launch and concluded
SCHEDULED_START. The new cause extends the vocabulary, which §5 gives as a
minimum; it is automatic and therefore non-invalidating, like a child restart.

C. Effective service timing is frozen or refused.
--poll-seconds changes wake cadence and --max-waits bounds service lifetime,
neither of which appears in a source-file digest - Blue's point that two services
from the same code with different arguments could share a fingerprint. Both are now
handled twice over: qualifying mode refuses them outright (cadence comes from the
frozen policy, and a qualifying service does not stop after N idle waits), and in
any mode the launcher exports its effective configuration so it is folded into the
fingerprint manifest under supervisor.effective_service_invocation. Restart delay,
restart burst limit and the qualifying flag itself are bound the same way.

Readiness now blocks on LAUNCH_NOT_SERVICE_MANAGED, NOT_QUALIFYING_SERVICE_MODE
and INVALIDATING_LIFECYCLE_CAUSE in addition to the unattested cause, so a
non-qualifying or manually started process cannot present itself as ready.

17 tests: omission never yields a scheduled start, a service-managed first launch
does, a dead supervisor is a supervisor restart and a clean prior exit is not,
child failure and deployment stay distinguishable, all five causes are classified,
claiming qualifying mode without a manager fails, an unrecognised manager is
rejected, readiness blocks unmanaged and manual launches, the launcher exits 2 on
each refused override, and cadence, lifetime bound, restart pacing and the
qualifying flag each move the fingerprint while identical environments agree.

263 tests pass.

subject: p0: close RETROSPECTIVE_AUDIT_CAN_FALSE_PASS with an obligation ledger
body:
p0: close RETROSPECTIVE_AUDIT_CAN_FALSE_PASS with an obligation ledger

Blue finding 1, accepted in full. All three sub-defects were confirmed in
audit.py at the verified head, and they shared one root cause: obligations had no
identity, so reconciliation was many-to-many.

The three false passes:
- the attempt window was `abs(attempt - due) <= tolerance`, whose second half
  subsumes the forward-only condition, so a request made before a deadline could
  be offered as proof that the deadline was later met;
- attempts were matched with `any(...)` and never consumed, so one request could
  answer several distinct obligations;
- an obligation counted as superseded by any later transition, including one
  recorded after the deadline had already been missed.

An obligation is now a named commitment. A transition that declares a
next_due_at_utc mints an obligation_id, and a transition that replaces a
still-open obligation names it in supersedes_obligation_id. The collector holds
open_obligation_id durably, so a restart cannot orphan a commitment the audit is
still expecting an answer for.

Exactly one resolution may retire an obligation:
- SUPERSEDED: a transition that names it, was recorded strictly before its due
  time, and carries a cause in AUTHORIZED_SUPERSESSION_CAUSES. Prospective by
  construction, so a post-hoc note cannot erase a hole. An unrecognised cause
  retires nothing, which is what keeps a future cause from silently clearing
  obligations.
- ATTEMPT: a durable attempt in [due, due + tolerance]. Forward only, and
  consumed - one attempt retires at most one obligation. Superseding transitions
  are consumed too, so one re-plan cannot retire two commitments.
- PENDING: the grace period has not elapsed yet, so the newest commitment of a
  live service is neither an answer nor a hole.

Supersessions resolve before attempts, because supersession is the stronger claim
and cannot be fabricated after the deadline; that ordering keeps scarce attempts
available for the obligations that actually needed a request. Either order is safe
against a false pass, and this one avoids spurious failures.

A transition that declared a due time without an obligation_id cannot be
reconciled by name. Rather than silently falling back to matching by time - the
defect being removed - the audit reports OBLIGATION_IDENTITY_MISSING and the
window fails.

14 adversarial tests. The three Blue cases are covered directly, plus: a late
attempt inside tolerance still answers, an attempt beyond tolerance does not, two
attempts answer two obligations, a prospective named supersession keeps the window
accountable, supersession without a named target or without an authorized cause
retires nothing, one transition cannot supersede two obligations, the four
statuses partition the ledger exactly, a live service's last obligation is pending
rather than a miss, and the production collector path emits a ledger the audit can
settle.

Verified discriminating: with the old matching semantics temporarily reinstated
inside the new module, 4 of these tests fail; with the correct semantics all 14
pass.

body:
p0: pre-t0 rodage, and the two defects it found

The rodage did its job: running the collector in the frozen state under the real
supervisor surfaced two defects that review and 231 offline tests had not.

DISCOVERY_FORM_TYPE_PREFIX_MATCH - BLOCKS_CAPTURE_INTEGRITY, closed
- EDGAR's Latest Filings `type` parameter is a prefix match, not an exact match:
  `type=4` also returns 497J/497K fund filings. The first live probe had simply
  landed on a window containing only form 4 entries.
- The anti-false-success guard is what exposed it. Three consecutive polls
  returned HTTP 200 and were refused as DISCOVERY_INVALID with
  COVERAGE_UNKNOWN rather than reported as NO_NEW_DATA. A collector that trusted
  the server filter would have logged three healthy quiet polls.
- Resolution: the server filter is a narrowing hint and local classification is
  authoritative. A form type outside the ownership set is excluded explicitly and
  inspectably via DiscoveryPage.excluded_form_types; a form type that is absent
  or not even shaped like an EDGAR form type remains an error, because that is
  the case where the filter genuinely cannot be shown to work. The known-fixture
  test remains the positive proof that Form 4s are surfaced.
- Query construction version bumped to v2 and the prefix semantics frozen in the
  manifest, so the fingerprint moved with the change.

FRESH_INSTALL_BOOT_FAILURE - pre-existing on the Blue base, closed
- On base commit c1a955316055aaf6c1b28853e21ed07e36e55f6a, QuantSystem.boot()
  raises TypeError on a clean var/. The insider_filings legacy entry had gained
  `acceptance` and `affected_subsystems` keys describing its capability gap, but
  only `capability` was filtered out of the ResearchTask kwargs.
- An already-seeded queue hid it: the seeding call short-circuits on the task id,
  so it reproduced only on a first boot - which is exactly when a new deployment
  of the capture service starts. It surfaced here because the canonical status
  replay always boots clean.
- Fixed by filtering an explicit BUILD_TASK_ONLY_FIELDS set, so a newly described
  gap cannot crash boot again, with a regression test that boots a fresh root.

Rodage evidence: handoff/SEC_FORM4_P0_PRE_T0_RODAGE_2026-09-18.json
- Two supervised service starts under deploy/quant_sec_supervisor.py, the second
  classified AUTOMATIC_RESTART_AFTER_FAILURE from supervisor state the collector
  cannot reach, with the acquisition fingerprint stable across the restart.
- Two validated polls, filings captured, coverage COMPLETE with no open gap, and
  a second poll that earned NO_NEW_DATA in one request with no refetch.
- The one-to-one invariant verified on live traffic: budget reservations ==
  durable attempt ids == distinct attempt ids.
- Retrospective audit accountable: no unexplained expected action, one stable
  fingerprint, every start externally attested.

Also adds continuous-service tests driving the real Control Plane clock: capture
wins the tick against genuinely due replayable work, quiet periods leave liveness
evidence, a stopped collector becomes observably stale without coverage being
upgraded, a missing requester identity is BLOCKED rather than healthy idle, a
capture fault is isolated without stopping the system, restart resumes without
mutating prior evidence, and the new scheduler/lifecycle/fingerprint surfaces are
firewall-safe with no contact address in the manifest.

The artifact states plainly what this rodage does not establish: multi-day
unattended operation, the required weekend and predeclared silence interval, live
429/403 behaviour (deliberately not provoked against SEC, proven offline only),
and multi-host budget coordination.

232 tests pass, schemas and status artifacts regenerate clean.

body:
p0: close both pre-t0 capture-integrity blockers and materialize fingerprint V1

Both BLOCKS_CAPTURE_INTEGRITY objects frozen in
governance/P0_ACQUISITION_CRITICAL_FINGERPRINT_V1.md are closed. t0 is not
declared and P0_CONTINUOUS_SERVICE_STATE is untouched: both belong to Blue.

HIDDEN_TRANSPORT_RETRY
- The nested HTTP retry in transport.py is removed. It could put two SEC
  requests under one limiter reservation and one attempt id, which understated
  real traffic as well as breaking the audit.
- The invariant is now structural rather than a property of reading the code:
  fetch() requires a single-use RequestPermit minted by the collector from one
  budget reservation and carrying the attempt id that will journal the outcome.
  The permit is consumed at the moment the request goes out, so a failure after
  the send can never be re-sent under the same reservation, and a second send
  raises PermitAlreadySpent.
- The ordinary cause of the failure the old retry papered over - a keep-alive
  socket the far end closed while the lane was idle - is handled by reconnecting
  *before* sending. A connection idle beyond idle_reuse_seconds is replaced
  during permit issue. That is the reconnect the governance explicitly permits:
  no extra request, no semantic change.
- The test FakeTransport honours the permit exactly as the real transport does,
  so all 117 lane tests exercise the invariant rather than only the ones naming
  it. assert_one_to_one checks requests == reservations == distinct attempt ids
  across a normal poll and drain, across pagination and reconciliation, and
  across every adverse path: transport error, hung request, 5xx, 429, 403,
  permanent 4xx, HTML-under-200 and truncated transfer. A source-level guard
  fails if a second request construct reappears in _fetch_once.

INCOMPLETE_CRITICAL_POLICY_SERIALIZATION
- A dedicated canonical serialization replaces to_dict(), which is a telemetry
  serializer with a different purpose and omitted filings_per_drain,
  accept_encoding and max_response_bytes - so two different acquisition policies
  could share a fingerprint.
- Completeness is by construction. Every SecAccessPolicy field carries exactly
  one classification; the three sets are pairwise disjoint and their union is
  checked against dataclasses.fields at generation time. An unclassified field
  raises UnclassifiedPolicyField and no fingerprint is produced, so it fails the
  build rather than only the tests. A classification for a removed field, and
  overlapping classifications, are rejected too.
- One field is EXPLICITLY_NONCRITICAL: sources, the SEC documentation provenance,
  with a frozen rationale and a test proving that recording a newer revision date
  leaves the fingerprint unchanged while an actual limit changed in response does
  move it.
- user_agent is bound as a non-plaintext digest, so the declared identity is
  covered without committing a contact address.

Fingerprint V1
- sha256(canonical_json(manifest)) over module digests, canonical policy, request
  shape including the literal query templates, the classification itself and the
  supervisor manifest. clock.py is included in full per the conservative V1 rule.
  supervisor.py and audit.py are included too: the audit cannot change collector
  behaviour, but a weakened audit could mask the hole a window exists to detect,
  and membership may only be narrowed before the first qualifying t0.
- Mutation matrix per the acceptance list: identical builds match; every
  INCLUDE_CANONICAL field is swept individually; timeouts, retry/backoff rules,
  discovery/coverage settings, declared identity, acquisition code and supervisor
  restart policy each move it; a downstream parser plus an unrelated desk change
  leave it unchanged.

Instrumentation
- Durable scheduler provenance: every cadence-changing transition records state,
  cause, next_due_at, the active fingerprint, boot id, lifecycle cause and
  backoff/cooldown, written prospectively so the audit never infers that nothing
  was due from the absence of an attempt. A blocked lane still declares its state
  with next_due_at null.
- Lifecycle provenance is read from the launcher, never self-attested. An absent
  or unrecognised cause is LIFECYCLE_CAUSE_UNATTESTED, an explicit provenance gap
  that readiness treats as not ready. MANUAL_START is flagged as invalidating.
- deploy/quant_sec_supervisor.py classifies why each instance started from state
  the collector cannot reach, and deploy/quant-sec-capture.service declares the
  restart policy; both are digested into the fingerprint.
- A retrospective audit reconciles declared due times against attempts and
  reports findings only. sec-serve, sec-fingerprint, sec-readiness and sec-audit
  are the operator entry points.

221 tests pass, schemas regenerate clean.

subject: p0: crash-boundary, request-control and firewall hardening, and state checkpoint
body:
p0: crash-boundary, request-control and firewall hardening, and state checkpoint

Checkpoint D, completing the mission's required test list. 177/177 tests pass,
schemas regenerate clean, and STATE.md / CHIEF_BRIEF.md are rebuilt from a
canonical replay rather than written by hand.

Crash boundaries, each killed at one specific commit point and then rebuilt
from disk exactly as a restart would:
- discovery to queue: the anchor has not moved, so the same work is rediscovered
  rather than skipped, and the identical discovery response deduplicates;
- raw write to envelope: bytes survive, no envelope means no acknowledgement,
  and the replay deduplicates instead of writing a second object;
- envelope to acknowledgement: a durable envelope means the filing is never
  fetched again, at zero requests and with no second envelope appended;
- acknowledgement to cursor advance: the cursor stays put, and the replay
  advances it without refetching.

That last test found a real bug. The deduplicated acknowledgement path dropped
its task but never advanced the cursor, so a crash followed by a replay could
leave the anchor stuck behind work that was provably complete. Replay is now an
acknowledgement like any other.

Also proven: disk-full during acquisition cannot acknowledge anything and
recovers cleanly once storage returns; a restart preserves the append-only
journals byte for byte along with cursor, coverage and an active cooldown.

Request controls under adverse responses: 429 honours Retry-After as a floor
above the policy minimum and stops draining immediately; 429 without one falls
back to the policy floor; 403 enters an extended cooldown and makes no further
request across repeated poll and drain attempts; timeouts and 5xx walk the
bounded 5s/15s/60s/5m/15m ladder with jitter and stop growing; a success resets
it; a hung request is HUNG_REQUEST with no invented receipt time and a still
diagnosable liveness state; a permanent 4xx is journalled without escalation;
a truncated filing transfer is never acknowledged and its partial bytes stay in
the incomplete namespace; the gzip path SEC actually uses hashes the wire bytes
at both discovery and filing. NO_NEW_DATA, REQUEST_FAILED and
COLLECTOR_DID_NOT_RUN are separable from the journal alone.

The visibility firewall is now executable and self-checked. Its detector is
first shown to flag a real Form 4, then pointed at every surface a
protocol-mutating actor can see - status surface, Chief Brief, event log,
exception text, snapshot JSON and the firewall-safe journals - all of which come
back clean while the restricted tier is confirmed to hold the identities. A
hostile feed whose form-type attribute embeds an accession and a transaction
field cannot get that text echoed into a reason class.

Control Plane: a capture fault is isolated like a research worker fault, so it
surfaces as SEC_CAPTURE FAULT with a durable attempt history rather than killing
the system or passing as a quiet poll. Five new JSON schemas are generated from
the capture dataclasses and covered by the existing drift check.

STATE.md records P0_RAW_CAPTURE_OPERATIONAL = TRUE with the live evidence, and
states the limits plainly: the traffic budget bounds one machine and cannot
coordinate two; capture history begins at its bootstrap point because the feed
is a rolling window, and repairing older gaps is the backfill engine's work;
captured bytes remain raw evidence with no parser and no admissibility, so
SCAN-INSIDER-FILINGS-001 stays scientifically blocked.

subject: p0: first real SEC probe, with the two bugs it exposed fixed
body:
p0: first real SEC probe, with the two bugs it exposed fixed

Checkpoint C. The collector made real SEC requests and the mission's acceptance
criteria are met by evidence rather than by assertion:

  VALID_DISCOVERY      = TRUE
  COVERAGE_STATE       = COMPLETE
  HEARTBEAT_DURABLE    = TRUE
  RAW_CAPTURE_DURABLE  = TRUE

SEC policy was re-checked against the authoritative pages before the first
request and is recorded in handoff/SEC_FORM4_P0_FIRST_LIVE_PROBE_2026-09-18.json
with the consulted URLs, their revision dates and the request controls in force.

What the probe produced: 22 requests under the 2 req/s global budget with
concurrency 1, one validated discovery page, 20 distinct Form-4 accessions
acquired as immutable raw objects, 22 objects re-hashed with no address
mismatch, and a second poll that earned NO_NEW_DATA by re-establishing
continuity from the cursor in a single request with no refetch. A restart
between the two polls preserved the attempt journal, envelopes, raw bytes,
cursor and coverage state.

Two real bugs the probe found, both now covered by tests.

1. SEC serves these endpoints gzip-encoded. Storing and hashing the exact wire
   bytes was correct, but the parse step was reading those stored bytes directly
   and failing as DISCOVERY_INVALID. Decoding is now a function applied to a
   verified copy read back through the content address, so parsing sees the
   decoded body while the stored object and its hash keep describing the bytes
   that arrived. The first probe's refusal to call an unparseable 200 NO_NEW_DATA
   is exactly the designed behaviour, and is what made the bug visible.

2. EDGAR's Latest Filings feed lists one accession once per filer, so a 40-entry
   page carried 20 distinct filings. Entry position would have queued each one
   twice; identity now deduplicates within a page as well as across polls. The
   immutable store had already absorbed the duplicate as a deduplication rather
   than an overwrite, which is why it cost nothing.

Two design corrections the probe motivated.

- Bootstrap is one page, not a crawl. The discovery feed is a rolling window
  with no beginning to walk back to, so the first poll defines where captured
  history starts and records that scope explicitly instead of implying full
  history. Anything older is the reconciliation/backfill engine's work.
- Acquisition is scheduled ahead of research and desk work. A missed discovery
  window is irrecoverable because a filing that leaves the rolling window cannot
  be observed at the time it was published, while research and desk work over
  committed fingerprinted data is replayable at any later tick. The first live
  run found the capture lane starved behind a 377-session desk backlog.

Control Plane integration: SEC_CAPTURE is a first-class logical function with
RUN/IDLE/BLOCKED state, driven by the existing clock as ordinary due work, with
no separate process. It fails closed when the SEC-required identity is absent -
BLOCKED with the remedy named, never a request. The declared User-Agent and
contact come from QUANT_SEC_USER_AGENT at runtime and are deliberately not
committed.

Visibility firewall is now executable rather than conventional: visibility.py
scans whatever a protocol-mutating actor can see for accession numbers, archive
paths, ownership XML, transaction fields, filer identities and raw markup. The
status surface, CHIEF_BRIEF section, telemetry and evidence artifact publish
states, times, opaque digests, byte totals and rate-limit state only. Filing
counts are withheld too, so work in flight is a boolean.

subject: p0: prove SEC discovery semantics and make coverage honest
body:
p0: prove SEC discovery semantics and make coverage honest

Checkpoint B: the two Astra P0 blockers, closed in code and tests, still with no
live request. Steady-state cost is one small discovery request per poll.

Discovery semantics (discovery.py)
- Latest Filings Ownership/Form-4 Atom feed for discovery and the pipe-delimited
  daily master index for coverage. Both are compact, purpose-built surfaces, so
  no CIK-by-CIK scan and no crawl around a filing: the raw document locator is
  derived deterministically from the accession, one request per filing.
- The parser refuses anything it cannot fully account for, because the failure
  being prevented is a silent NO_NEW_DATA on a broken response. HTML served with
  a nominal 200, non-XML, a non-Atom root, a feed missing its title/updated/link
  markers, an entry without a form type, a form type the request did not ask for,
  an unrecognised locator, disagreeing accession identities, and more entries
  than the window requested are all DISCOVERY_INVALID.
- Entries carry accession, form type, CIK, locators and the source publication
  time only. No title, issuer, owner or summary: a field that does not exist
  cannot leak.

Anti-false-success (collector.py)
- NO_NEW_DATA is earned, never defaulted. assert_no_new_data_earned is the single
  guard: it requires a validated discovery response and proven continuity, and
  raises if either is missing or if new items were found.

Coverage truthfulness
- Continuity means this poll walked back to the exact identity the last validated
  poll reached. That anchor is also the dedup short-circuit, so in steady state
  the walk stops on page one and an already-acknowledged identity costs zero
  requests.
- Everything else is COVERAGE_UNKNOWN with the affected cursor/page range or day
  recorded durably: the anchor falling out of the rolling window, the page budget
  exhausted mid-overflow, a page that failed or would not parse, and a poll cut
  short by a restart. Offsets into a live feed are not stable across a restart,
  so a partial walk is not resumed in place; the range is recorded unknown and
  the next successful walk from the unadvanced anchor resolves it by proof.
- A healthy heartbeat never upgrades coverage: with any gap open, coverage stays
  COVERAGE_UNKNOWN however well the poll went.
- The daily index is the coverage authority. Expected Form-4 accessions for a
  closed day are compared against what was captured; a shortfall opens a durable
  gap. Day-1 is honest detection, so the backfill engine remains later work. An
  unavailable or unparseable index never confirms coverage.

Crash-safe ordering
- Raw bytes, then envelope, then task acknowledgement, then cursor advance. The
  cursor's next position is held durably so the advance survives a restart

subject: p0: immutable SEC raw store, acquisition journals and global traffic budget
body:
p0: immutable SEC raw store, acquisition journals and global traffic budget

Checkpoint A of the P0 SEC/Form-4 raw-capture mission: the Day-1 irreversible
layer, offline and tested, before any discovery semantics or live request.

Frozen access policy (src/quant/dataplane/sec/policy.py)
- SEC fair-access documentation re-checked against the authoritative pages and
  recorded as data, with the consulted URL, the page's own revision date and
  the local date of the re-check, so a test can assert the implementation never
  exceeds what the source permits.
- Fails closed: no default User-Agent, and a declared identity without a contact
  address is rejected. A shared placeholder would make every deployment look
  identical to the SEC, which is the opposite of what the guidance asks for.
- Conservative by design: 60s discovery poll, concurrency 1, 2 req/s, no burst,
  bounded 5s/15s/60s/5m/15m backoff ladder with jitter.

Global SEC traffic budget (budget.py)
- Keyed on a file, not an instance, so a second SEC consumer added later cannot
  collectively exceed the frozen rate. The advisory lock is the concurrency cap.
- The spacing timestamp is persisted before the request leaves, so a process
  killed mid-request cannot re-spend the slot.
- Cooldowns are durable and extend-only: restarting cannot shorten a cooldown
  the source asked for. Retry-After is parsed in both permitted forms.

Transport (transport.py)
- http.client with a reused keep-alive connection: no TLS handshake per filing,
  and no library that silently decodes Content-Encoding. The hash always
  describes the bytes that arrived, and decoding happens on a throwaway copy
  only to parse.
- Completeness is provable or the response is not a capture: declared
  Content-Length is compared against what was read, a premature end of a
  chunked body is TRUNCATED rather than a short success, and a whole-request
  deadline stops a trickling response from stalling liveness.
- Exception text carries error classes only, never response content, because
  logs are inside the visibility firewall.

Immutable store and journals (store.py)
- Content-addressed objects linked into place rather than renamed, so an
  existing object cannot be clobbered even under a race, and stored 0o444.
- Identical re-capture deduplicates; differing bytes under one source identity
  append an explicit conflict version instead of replacing anything.
- Truncated transfers are preserved in a separate incomplete namespace and can
  never be promoted to a valid capture.
- Acknowledgement is the durable envelope, which is what makes each crash
  boundary replayable.
- Two journal tiers: the firewall-safe tier carries opaque locator digests only,
  while plaintext locators, accessions and source publication times live in a
  restricted tier no status surface reads. Point-in-time reconstructability is
  preserved without giving the firewall-safe tier anything interpretable.

28 offline tests cover exact-byte store/reload, duplicate and conflicting bytes,
read-only objects, corruption detection, incomplete namespacing, disk-full,
attempt/receipt timestamp separation, source-time vs receipt-time, locator
firewall, rate spacing, cross-consumer budget sharing, durable cooldown,
backoff ladder, Retry-After, and compressed/truncated transfer semantics.

  census. Malformed lines are attributed to an accession and excluded; a
  malformed line with no recoverable accession fails the build.
- Two-phase build: the submission/owner identity universe is frozen across
  all quarters before any transaction row is normalized, so no certified
  output can depend on quarter, member or line order.
- Compact SubmissionRecord/ReportingOwnerRecord projections limit the
  certified read surface to the declared columns.

  waterfall/ledger, EDGAR document identity, cache promotion, torn tail,

subject: feat: durable, checkpointable EDGAR acceptance resolution
body:
feat: durable, checkpointable EDGAR acceptance resolution

EDGAR acceptance resolution is the long pole of the census: ~31,000 documents
at SEC's fair-access pace. Previously it was a single sequential loop whose only
durability was an unvalidated file cache, so an interruption anywhere cost the
whole pass and a corrupted cache entry was trusted on sight.

Resolution is now durable and resumable, and may optionally run several workers.
Concurrency is admissible here only because three properties hold together, and
each is asserted by test rather than assumed:

- One process-global token-bucket rate limiter. Fair Access is a property of the
  process, not of a thread, so every worker draws from the same bucket and the
  pace does not scale with worker count. The default bucket holds a single
  token, so a run cannot open with a burst above its declared pace.
- Disjoint accession assignment. Work is strided across shards deterministically,
  so no document is ever fetched twice.
- Atomic cache writes plus a batched checkpoint carrying each document's sha256,
  byte count and parsed acceptance time. A kill at any instant resumes exactly.

Resume validates rather than trusts. A checkpoint entry whose cached bytes no
longer hash as recorded, or whose file is gone, is not resumed: it is fetched
again. A tampered document can still parse, so hash validation is what prevents
altered content being laundered into the census. A checkpoint line torn by a
kill is ignored rather than partially believed.

The resolved mapping is assembled from the sorted accession list, so the result
is identical whatever the worker count or completion order. Existing cached
documents are revalidated and back-filled into the checkpoint without refetching.

Two concurrency defects in this implementation were found by the new tests and
fixed before use:

- The checkpoint buffer was appended under one lock and drained under another.
  Guarding one list with two locks loses records appended between reading the
  payload and clearing the list, which would leave completed work absent from
  the checkpoint and silently re-fetched on resume.
- The limiter's default bucket held a full second of tokens, so a run opened
  with a burst at roughly twice its declared pace. Fair Access concerns the pace
  actually presented to the service, so the default is now a single token.

Defaults are unchanged behaviour: one worker, and a rate well under SEC's
published guidance. Concurrency is opt-in through --workers, and --rate-per-second
is a process-wide budget independent of it.

Adds tests/test_sec_edgar_resolver.py (14 tests): worker count does not change
the result, failures are reported in a stable order, no accession is fetched
twice, shards partition exactly, the rate limit is global rather than per worker,
a single limiter paces every thread, atomic replacement is all-or-nothing, a
concurrent reader never observes a partial document, an interrupted run refetches
exactly the outstanding accessions, resume equals an uninterrupted run, every
checkpoint entry carries a verifiable hash, altered or missing bytes are not
resumed, and a torn checkpoint line is ignored.

159 tests pass. No census definition, population, threshold, window or
scientific semantic is touched.

subject: ci: make the census gate resumable across runs
body:
ci: make the census gate resumable across runs

Measured against the live service, the gate cannot finish in one job. The raw
SEC inputs are 26 quarterly ZIPs plus one EDGAR acceptance header per accession
in event lineage. That lineage is ~31,500 accessions, estimated twice by an
independent method: the resolver walks the accession list in sorted order, so
the resolved set is a prefix of it, and the share of all 1,192,982 original
Form-4 accessions sorting below the highest resolved accession gives the
position. Two measurements two hours apart returned ~32,900 and ~31,500.

At SEC's fair-access pace that is roughly six hours of fetching, longer than the
maximum job duration. The previous 330-minute budget could not have completed a
cold run regardless of the identity repair, which is a second reason the gate
kept failing.

Acquisition now restores var/sec_form4_raw before it runs and saves it even when
the job fails or times out, so successive runs resume rather than restart. The
cached payloads are immutable published SEC documents and each still carries its
own sha256 in the provenance manifest, so resuming does not weaken the proof:
the bytes are still the bytes SEC served, and the manifest still proves it.

Raises the job budget to the 360-minute ceiling.

Known limitation for Red Team: with a cold cache the gate needs two runs to go
green, the first banking partial acquisition and the second completing it. This
is a property of the source's pace, not of the census definition.

No census definition, population, threshold, window or scientific semantic is
touched.

subject: fix: one SEC HTTP identity for preflight and acquisition
body:
fix: one SEC HTTP identity for preflight and acquisition

The V2-A gate failed with a green connectivity preflight and a refused
acquisition. The cause was never the runner or the network: the preflight and
the Python acquisition derived their HTTP identity from different places, so
they were two different clients and only one of them was acceptable to SEC.

Root cause, established by probing the official 2020Q1 URL directly:

  ...@gmail.com                                  -> 200
  noreply@gmail.com                              -> 200
  ...@users.noreply.github.com                   -> 403
  ...@github.com                                 -> 403
  ...@gmail.com https://github.com/owner/repo    -> 403

SEC refuses any User-Agent containing "github.com", and refuses any declaration
without a contact address. The gate exported
"Quant-Trade <actor>@users.noreply.github.com https://github.com/<repo>", which
contains it twice, so it could not have succeeded on any runner class. The 403
body reads "Request Rate Threshold Exceeded", which reads as a rate limit but is
a compliance rejection. Header sets are irrelevant: the same request succeeds
with minimal or full headers once the declaration is acceptable.

Changes, transport only. No census definition, population, threshold, window or
scientific semantic is touched.

- sec_user_agent() is the single source of truth for the declared identity, and
  sec_request_headers() is the single source of truth for the header set. There
  is deliberately no committed default: one would either embed a personal
  contact address in a public repository or invent an unreachable one, and an
  unreachable contact is not Fair-Access compliance. An undeclared identity now
  fails immediately with an actionable message instead of a misleading 403.
- sec_identity_problem() encodes both empirical refusal rules, so a bug class
  found by evidence is now an automated invariant rather than a matter of future
  vigilance.
- _http_get() resolves the identity per call. Its previous default argument was
  bound at import time, which froze the identity before the environment was read
  and is itself a way to reintroduce the divergence.
- The CI preflight now runs scripts/sec_form4_census.py --preflight, which calls
  the acquisition path itself, so a preflight can no longer pass while the
  acquisition it validates is refused. The runner returns to ubuntu-latest and
  the identity comes from a secret.
- 403 and 404 are no longer retried. A 404 is an absent object and a 403 is a
  compliance rejection; retrying either only delays a deterministic failure.

Second defect found while verifying the full window: the hardcoded year boundary
sent 2026Q1 to the wrong official root. SEC serves 2026Q1 from the legacy root
and only 2026Q2 from the newer one, so acquisition would have 404'd mid-window.
Quarters now resolve against both official SEC roots in a deterministic order
and provenance records which root actually served each quarter. Both roots are
the same publisher; this is not a mirror or a substitute source.

Verified: all 26 quarters 2020Q1-2026Q2 acquired from official SEC roots,
280,647,670 bytes, 2020Q1 sha256
3c3bc3fefa4dbe32cb68f052ac4ea32cae16099bb2b104a0bd8d242465e004a8.

Adds tests/test_sec_form4_identity.py (13 tests) covering the undeclared, the
no-contact and the github.com refusal cases, that the identity is not frozen at
import time, that preflight, quarterly acquisition and EDGAR acceptance fetches
send byte-identical headers, that the workflow declares no identity of its own
and that its declaration would not itself be refused. The 28 existing census
tests still pass.

Also commits the pinned XNYS session calendar (exchange_calendars 4.13.1) used
by the frozen 10-session window.

subject: Corrective integrity pass: one causal timeline, crash-idempotent state, sleeves
body:
Corrective integrity pass: one causal timeline, crash-idempotent state, sleeves

Repairs the six integrity defects found by independent review of PR #12. The V1
implementation is preserved; no new research lanes, markets or architecture.

1. One causal market timeline
   Research measured close(t) -> close(t+1) while the desk filled at open(t+1),
   so every published metric credited the overnight gap between the decision and
   the earliest possible fill. The desk was worse: it applied fills priced at
   open(t+1) and then marked the Book at close(t), moving economic state
   backward in time. Research, execution and marking now share one timeline:
   information through close(t) -> decision after close(t) -> entry at
   open(t+1) -> exit and mark at open(t+2) or later. The adjusted price basis
   moves onto the panel so all three read it identically. Marking backward now
   raises; repeating a mark restates the session instead of inventing one.

2. Crash-idempotent economic state
   Fills carry deterministic operation ids and replay is a no-op. Operation ids
   alone were not sufficient: a replay after a partial crash re-decided against
   an already-mutated Book, saw no drift and recorded NO_TRADE, leaving the
   money right and the history wrong. A session that is about to move money now
   records its intent in a write-ahead desk journal, so a restart re-applies the
   original decision instead of making a new one. Desk counters moved into that
   journal so an outcome and its bookkeeping commit in one durable write.

3. Strategy sleeves
   Positions are keyed by (strategy, symbol). Two strategies can hold opposing
   exposure in one instrument without overwriting attribution. Portfolio state
   is the computed aggregate of the sleeves.

4. IDLE means alive
   Adds `serve`: work when work is due, wait when it is not, wake on due work or
   on data that arrived while waiting. Time is injectable, so liveness is tested
   deterministically. The dataset registry now reloads from disk, without which
   a long-running clock could never notice a dataset another process registered.

5. RISK validates the final simulated state
   A strategy is no longer charged twice for the sleeve it already holds. The
   verdict describes the post-scale portfolio, and the executed portfolio is
   re-checked after capacity truncation. Scaling answers only the size limits
   (gross, drawdown throttle); a neutrality or concentration breach is
   structural and is vetoed rather than quietly resized. The scale is found by
   search, because scaling cannot shrink exposure held by other sleeves and a
   closed-form ratio of proposed gross was wrong.

6. Watchdog
   RUNNING is not STUCK. Tasks carry a start time and a lease; only an expired
   lease is reported stuck. Work with no recorded start is treated as stale,
   which is the conservative direction.

Recomputed research results, replacing the superseded PR #12 numbers
   Under the corrected timeline the daily cross-sectional family no longer
   survives its own discovery window: best Sharpe -0.015 against +0.20 before,
   so the validation window was preserved rather than spent. Most of its
   apparent edge was in the forbidden interval. The execution-aware lane still
   reaches validation and is still rejected: -6.08% net, -1.37% gross, 32.9x
   turnover, beta -0.062, t = -0.39 against a required 3.20 after 36 declared
   expressions. No strategy is tradable; the capital Book has never taken a
   position. The counterfactual evaluation ledger stands at -0.62% over 377
   sessions and 518 modelled fills, scored UNDETERMINED.

Verification
   82 tests and a 35-assertion demonstration, including an overnight-gap fixture
   where all apparent return sits in the forbidden interval, crash injection at
   the dangerous boundary proving crash+restart+replay equals the uninterrupted
   run across cash, sleeves, fills, attribution, NAV and session history,
   opposing multi-strategy ownership of one symbol, deterministic liveness, a
   scaling regression against existing book exposure, and healthy-versus-stale
   watchdog cases.

Truthfulness
   STATE.md and README no longer claim decay management the system has never
   exercised; superseded strategy versions are actually retained, so the
   registry is version-preserving in fact. Assumed rather than calibrated
   execution costs are labelled as such.
